nodes.title: Continuous batching
nodes.text: Admit new sequences when existing sequences finish. Token scheduling improves accelerator utilization; admission limits prevent a long queue from exhausting memory.

nodes.title: KV cache budget
nodes.text: Attention keys and values are retained for previous tokens. Estimate bytes from layers, sequence length, key value heads, head dimension, concurrency and element precision.

nodes.title: Prefill and decode
nodes.text: Prompt prefill processes input tokens together. Autoregressive decode emits one new token per sequence per step. Time to first token and time between tokens describe different bottlenecks.

nodes.title: Weight quantization
nodes.text: Low bit weight representations reduce parameter storage. Calibration, group size and quantization error affect quality. Weight precision alone does not determine KV cache precision or total device memory.

nodes.title: On-device deployment
nodes.text: Local model execution must fit memory and supported operators while meeting latency, thermal and battery constraints. Test the target device, model artifact and runtime together.

nodes.title: Model routing
nodes.text: Choose a model using task requirements, latency budget and capability checks. A smaller model is useful only if it meets the acceptance criteria. Record router decisions and fallback reasons.

nodes.title: Admission control
nodes.text: Bound in-flight work and queue length. Reject or defer excess requests before the service loses its latency objective. Account for prompt lengths rather than counting requests alone.

nodes.title: Bounded retry
nodes.text: Retry transient failures with a deadline, backoff and jitter. Repeated attempts must fit the remaining budget. Retrying non-idempotent side effects can duplicate an action.

nodes.title: Idempotency keys
nodes.text: An operation key lets a service recognize duplicate attempts and return the prior outcome. Persist the outcome and request identity across process restarts when side effects matter.

nodes.title: Distributed traces
nodes.text: Correlate request, retrieval, tool, model and validation spans. Preserve parent identifiers, errors and retry attempts. A trace records execution evidence but does not establish answer correctness.

nodes.title: Latency distributions
nodes.text: Measure p50, p95 and p99 under representative concurrency and input lengths. Separate queue wait, preparation, model execution and streaming. Report warmup and hardware alongside results.

nodes.title: Canary release
nodes.text: Release to a bounded cohort and compare quality, error and latency signals with a baseline. Define stop conditions, monitor delayed feedback and keep a compatible rollback artifact.

nodes.title: Artifact registry
nodes.text: Version model weights, tokenizer, runtime, prompt, dataset and evaluator. A release manifest ties their identities together. Checksums identify bytes rather than proving quality.

nodes.title: Rollback compatibility
nodes.text: Restore a prior compatible model and application configuration. Data migrations, feature schemas and runtime operators can prevent a simple artifact rollback. Exercise recovery before a release.

nodes.title: Lexical retrieval baseline
nodes.text: BM25 ranks documents using query term overlap, inverse document frequency and length normalization. It is a strong cheap baseline for exact names and terminology; no training judgments are needed.

nodes.title: Dense retrieval
nodes.text: A text encoder maps queries and documents to vectors. Similarity can retrieve semantic matches without exact words. Pin encoder revision, chunking and index settings; evaluate on held-out queries.

nodes.title: Candidate reranking
nodes.text: A second stage scores a bounded candidate set with a query and each document. Candidate recall bounds final ranking quality. Compare extra latency and quality against the first-stage baseline.

nodes.title: Document chunking
nodes.text: Split documents with stable identifiers and useful boundaries. Retain headings and provenance. Very small chunks can lose context; very large chunks can dilute matching and exceed context budgets.

nodes.title: Citation validation
nodes.text: Check that answer citations refer to supplied source identifiers. Identifier membership is not entailment. A separate claim-to-evidence review must assess whether the cited text actually supports each claim.

nodes.title: Grounded answer evaluation
nodes.text: Evaluate factual claims against retrieved evidence. Separate retrieval failures from reader failures, unsupported claims and wrong citations. Human adjudication is useful when automated judges disagree.

nodes.title: Retrieval recall
nodes.text: Recall at k measures the fraction of judged relevant items retrieved within k results. Candidate recall measures whether later reranking can possibly recover the desired evidence.

nodes.title: Graded ranking quality
nodes.text: Normalized discounted cumulative gain rewards highly relevant documents near the top of a ranking. Define relevance grades, logarithmic discount and cutoff. Missing judgments can bias evaluation.

nodes.title: Leakage-aware splits
nodes.text: Keep paraphrases and shared intent groups in one split. Select checkpoints on validation only. A temporal test excludes future information; a held-out query test on a known graph is not unseen-graph generalization.

nodes.title: Uncertainty estimates
nodes.text: Bootstrap query-level metric rows to show sensitivity to sampled questions. Fixed-model intervals omit training-seed uncertainty and do not prove significance. Compare paired query outcomes when testing differences.

nodes.title: Graph schema
nodes.text: Define node identity, relation direction, edge confidence, source and availability time before model training. Derived reverse edges inherit the original evidence availability. A graph database stores relationships without requiring a neural model.

nodes.title: Message passing
nodes.text: A graph neural network transforms neighbor features, aggregates incoming messages and updates each node representation. Relation-specific parameters can distinguish prerequisite, mitigation and measurement links.

nodes.title: Graph convolution
nodes.text: A GCN mixes self and neighbor features with symmetric degree normalization and a learned projection. Repeated propagation expands the receptive field and may blur distinctions between nodes.

nodes.title: Neighbor sampling
nodes.text: GraphSAGE learns an aggregator over sampled neighbors and combines neighborhood evidence with a node self representation. Sampling controls memory and computation but introduces estimator variability.

nodes.title: Graph attention
nodes.text: Attention assigns normalized neighbor coefficients from node features. GATv2 allows the query node to change neighbor ranking. Attention coefficients describe computation and are not causal explanations.

nodes.title: Oversmoothing diagnostic
nodes.text: Repeated aggregation can make node representations similar. Inspect feature variance, task quality and receptive field as depth grows. Residual connections help optimization but do not guarantee informative representations.

nodes.title: Temporal graph snapshots
nodes.text: Filter nodes and edges by evidence availability at the prediction cutoff. Exclude future events and reverse-edge leakage. Publication or ingestion time can differ from the event time recorded inside a document.

nodes.title: Graph evidence for an LLM
nodes.text: Retrieve a compact connected evidence set from a knowledge graph, then pass readable text and source identifiers to a language model. Graph retrieval can use traversal or learned ranking; GraphRAG does not imply a GNN.

nodes.title: Evidence trust boundary
nodes.text: Treat retrieved text as untrusted data. Keep system instructions outside evidence, restrict tool permissions and validate outputs. A disclaimer inside a prompt alone does not prevent prompt injection.

nodes.title: Relation semantics
nodes.text: Connected nodes need not share a label. Distinguish incompatible relation types and edge directions. A graph model can fail when it assumes homophily but edges represent complementary roles.

nodes.title: Graph ablation
nodes.text: Compare trained graph ranking with lexical search, graph diffusion and a feature-only neural model. Removing edges with weights fixed measures sensitivity; retraining without edges is a separate experiment.

nodes.title: Cold-start evidence
nodes.text: New documents can have text but no graph links. Preserve a lexical or dense fallback, measure isolated-node behavior and separate unseen-node evaluation from unseen-query evaluation.

nodes.title: Future runtime proposal
nodes.text: This fictional runtime proposal is unavailable until 2027. It exists only to exercise temporal exclusion and must not appear in September 2026 evidence.
